newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia faces A$640 mln budget shortfall - paper.
newsitem.headline: Australia faces A$640 mln budget shortfall - paper.

text.p: The Australian government faced a A$640 million 1996/97 budget shortfall with tax collection from small business running below projections, The Australian Financial Review newspaper reported on Wednesday.
The paper, citing Tax Office documents, said the shortfall prompted tax authorities to tighten monitoring of small businesses.

The paper said the Tax Office assessment, in an internal report on small business income for February, was based on figures after Treasurer Peter Costello said in January's mid-year review of budget and economic forecasts that total company tax receipts would be about A$1.6 billion below budget estimates.
The details in the latest assessment suggested "the shortfall in overall company tax collections could be even bigger than feared in January", the Review said.
Australia's budget is expected to produce an underlying deficit -- excluding asset sales and state government debt repayments -- of A$8.5 billion in the fiscal year to June 30, 1997.
Costello is due to announce the 1997/98 budget on May 13.
Prime Minister John Howard said on Tuesday had a big effort ahead of it as it worker on meeting its budget targets.
Canberra has targeted an underlying budget balance in 1998/99.
